source.title: Reliable Unlearning Harmful Information in LLMs with Metamorphosis Representation Projection
source.authors: Chengcan Wu; Ze-Ming Wei; Huan-Ran Chen; Yin-Peng Dong; Meng Sun

page_placements.theme: Forgotten knowledge re-emerges through later non-adversarial updates

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests similar-data relearning attacks against several unlearning methods and its proposed method, and argues that common methods can mask rather than erase knowledge while MRP resists the tested attack.
record.gate_note: The paper also cites prior relearning and jailbreak attacks, but those cited results are not rows. Its reported overall unlearning scores are composite scores rather than direct targeted-knowledge accuracies, so they are not recorded as near-chance accuracy results. No activation-direction ablation, quantization attack, or prompting-only recovery test is reported.
record.test_reason: Section 5.4 runs a similar-data relearning attack on GA, EUL, NPO, RMU and O3. Unlearn accuracy rises from below 0.4 to about 0.5, and the authors argue these methods mask rather than erase. The paper's own method, MRP, is offered as a robust counter-method and stays below 0.4 after the same attack.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that fine-tuning-based unlearning masks rather than erases knowledge, leaving it recoverable by similar-data relearning and degraded by continual unlearning. They conclude MRP's projections resist the tested relearning attack and support continual unlearning while preserving retain performance.
record.recipe_differences: MRP uses projection matrices on hidden representations and tests relearning with similar but distinct same-topic data; it is not a reproduction of the original unlearning methods or their evaluation recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported relearning outcome depends on the unlearning method and relearning epoch; the paper reports aggregate baseline outcomes and does not give a full per-method numerical breakdown in the text.

fits_no_version.finding: In continual unlearning, unlearning later tasks revives earlier forgotten knowledge. GA's Task 1 accuracy rebounds from 0.363 to 0.411 and then 0.447 (Table 1). Baselines drift toward Origin accuracy across four tasks (Fig. 3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Recovery by subsequent unlearning: sequential unlearning of other tasks partially restores previously unlearned knowledge.

record.problems: The robustness test uses similar but distinct data from the same biology topic, and the relearning-set size is not stated. Baseline attack outcomes are mostly reported as aggregate textual summaries rather than per-method numerical values. Experiments are described on 7B models; the paper notes that scaling to larger models remains untested.
record.rows_left_out: Tables 2–10 report composite unlearning/retention scores and hyperparameter outcomes, not direct targeted-knowledge recovery measures for the claim versions. The plotted per-method curves in Figures 3–4 are not separately transcribed because the accompanying text does not state the individual values.

untested.parts: General-capability benchmarks beyond ScienceQA language and social science; attacks other than similar-data fine-tuning.
Unrelated relearning data; a subset of the forgotten facts; stated relearning-set size; models other than LLaMA2-7B for the attack.
All: no direction ablation or blocked-vs-deleted analysis. The 'masking' claim is inferred only from relearning.
All: no rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context attack.
Robustness of MRP to internal edits, quantization, prompting attacks, larger relearning sets, and models other than LLaMA2-7B.

missing.what: GA Task 1 QA accuracy rebound during continual unlearning (0.640 to 0.363, then 0.411 and 0.447)
Per-method unlearn and retain accuracy curves under the relearning attack, and MRP's pre-relearn accuracy
Baselines approach Origin accuracy and O3 falls below random (0.27 vs 0.31) in continual unlearning

record.verdict_notes: The reader used invalid version ids (V1, V2, V6); these are remapped to A, B and F. The R1, R2 and R6 results are the study's own method, so they are linked to F, not A. Baseline attack results are aggregate textual statements. The Qwen and WMDP results are composite scores only, with no relearning attack. Only 7B models were tested. The relearn-set size is not given.

versions.untested_parts: The robustness attack tested is similar-data fine-tuning only; no separate attack-tested general capability benchmark is reported.

The relearning examples are similar but distinct categories from the same biology topic. The relearning-set size is not stated; unrelated examples and a specified small subset of forgotten facts are not tested.
No activation-direction ablation or direct experiment distinguishing blocked access from deletion is reported.
No low-bit quantization attack is reported.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual, or in-context-only recovery attack is reported.
MRP is tested against similar-data fine-tuning relearning only, not against internal edits, quantization, or prompting-only attacks.

source_check.condition: Baseline methods (GA, EUL, NPO, RMU, O3; aggregate) on LLaMA2-7B, Genes to traits, under same-topic relearning
source_check.reason: A says simple attacks don't recover the knowledge. One epoch of same-topic fine-tuning lifts most baselines from below 0.4 (random 0.35) to above 0.45, and to about 0.5 after 5 (R4, R5). The authors state the methods mask rather than erase. The partial size of the recovery bears on B (l1). A's no-recovery property fails, shown by a number and stated explicitly. Values are aggregates over 'most methods'.

relation.reason: Section 5.4 runs relearning attacks on baselines and on MRP.

tranche.reason: The paper argues from its own relearning results that fine-tuning-based unlearning masks knowledge, and it also shows a counter-method.

source_check.notes: Baseline relearning results are aggregates over 'most methods' (per-method values only in Figure 4). Original accuracy on Genes to traits and MRP's pre-relearn accuracy are not stated. MRP trains only about 0.1M projection parameters, applied by hook (Table 5, Alg. 1). The text does not say which parameters, learning rate or data size the relearning attack uses, and removing the projection is not tested.

statements.correction: LLaMA2-7B, ScienceQA, unlearn Genes to traits, relearn on same-topic Classification and Heredity data: most baselines go from below 0.4 (random 0.35) to above 0.45 after 1 epoch and about 0.5 after 5 (0.506 in intro). Authors: the methods mask rather than erase. Original accuracy on Genes to traits not stated; biology Task 1 Origin is 0.640 in Table 1 (continual GA setup). Retain accuracy also rises after relearning.
statements.problem: The statement lists this study's same-topic biology QA among cases where loosely related text gives 'modest or no recovery', under a challenges label for B. The study reports clear but partial recovery, and the authors read it as masking, not erasure. This study's own B verdict is limits_scope, not challenges.

statements.correction: MRP (preprint with code, the method authors' own test), LLaMA2-7B, ScienceQA: after unlearning Genes to traits and 5 epochs of relearning on same-topic Classification and Heredity data, unlearn accuracy is 0.383 (random 0.35; baselines about 0.5). After four consecutive natural-science unlearns, 0.30 vs random 0.31. With only language science as retain training, social-science retain accuracy drops by less than 0.05 (App. D.3). Only this one relearning attack was tested.
statements.problem: The statement cites R1, R2 and R6 but gives no result for this study. Its conditions (1B-3B Llama/Qwen, Zephyr; TOFU, LKF, FaithUn, WMDP-cyber; mostly one epoch) and its 'why' list do not cover MRP's LLaMA2-7B ScienceQA setting. Supporting F is right in direction.

statements.correction: GA Task 1 QA accuracy: Origin 0.640, 0.363 after Task 1, 0.411 after Task 2, 0.447 after Task 3 (Table 1, LLaMA2-7B, ScienceQA).
